entries.english:
(Co-)Plaintiffs / applicants / interveners: several residents of the villages of Aufenau and Neudorf (called Neuendorf in the file) (power of attorney with 52 signatures).
(Co-)Defendants / interveners: the brothers and cousins Forstmeister von Gelnhausen (power of attorney from Johann Philipp Friedrich Forstmeister von Gelnhausen, chamberlain of the Electorate of Mainz and Oberamtmann zu Hausen, Orb und Burgjoß, and Wilhelm Friedrich Forstmeister von Gelnhausen).
Plaintiff’s attorneys: Lic. Ambrosius Joseph Stephani and (substitute) Lic. Johann Melchior Deuren (1732).
Defendant’s attorneys: Lic. Franz Peter Jung and (substitute) Lic. Johann Leonhard Krifft (1732).
Contemporary subject of dispute: A summons to hear the grievances presented and removed, and to grant the petitioners, as free persons, relief from the imposition of undefined labor services and unlawful dues, and to order restitution with costs and all related consequences.
Modern subject of dispute: Dispute over small labor services. The plaintiffs appeal to the Imperial Chamber Court because the defendants demanded unmeasured services instead of the customary measured ones, including carting over long distances, lengthy labor, and work on the Forstmeister estate at Wirtheim; treated them as serfs liable to provide the best head of livestock; took communal land from them; and exempted purchased farmsteads from their former matricular assessment. The defendants claim that unmeasured labor services were customary, especially since their subjects had no property of their own in the woods and pastures and could use them only through the lords’ indulgence. After the defendants arrested two subjects for refusing labor service and prohibited access to water and pasture, the plaintiffs also obtained a mandatum de cassando inhibitionem s. c.
Proceedings: Imperial Chamber Court, 1732–1808 (1732–1735).

Contents include: a list of labor services owed by the community members of Aufenau and Neudorf as fiefholders of Rodenstein (item 4); permissions to marry and move away issued by the Forstmeister court and office at Aufenau, 1692–1729 (item 6); exhibits to the plea of exception (item 8): a list of Martin Forstmeister von Gelnhausen’s rights at Aufenau and Neudorf (no. 1); extracts from a Forstmeister manual (1533) and accounts (1597–1719) concerning forest dues, departure dues, and the best head of livestock (nos. 2, 8, 9); an undated petition by the plaintiffs describing obligations to the manorial lord (no. 3); an extract from the Aufenau court record of 1660 (no. 4); an Imperial Chamber Court mandate in the case of Hans Dietrich von Rosenberg, councillor of the Electorate of Mainz, as guardian of the three sons of Lukas Forstmeister von Gelnhausen, and Philipp Reichard Forstmeister von Gelnhausen, against Count Wolfgang Ernst von Isenburg-Büdingen and Peter Bott, his forester in the Büdinger Forest, concerning woodcutting rights there, 1623 (no. 5); the reverses of Friedrich Hoffmann of Neudorf and Velten Scharpf of Aufenau concerning labor and other obligations, 1591 (no. 6); witness statements before a notary, 1732 (items 9, 24); orders from Georg Friedrich von Rodenstein to his subjects at Aufenau and Neudorf to render only the customary dues to the defendant family, or not to let themselves be kept from hearing the Gospel, 1655 and 1667 (items 12, 13); a notarial instrument of 1732 containing three agreements between the Amtmann at Orb and subjects at Aufenau concerning the purchase of brushwood, 1718–1725 (item 23); extracts from the Forstmeister division register of 1567 and Forstmeister registers concerning income from interest at Aufenau and Neudorf, 1532–1562 (item 25, letters D–I); an extract from a Forstmeister account concerning income from pig-grazing, 1714 (item 35); a letter from Lukas the Younger to Lukas the Elder Forstmeister von Gelnhausen concerning complaints by the subjects at Aufenau and Neudorf, 1598 (item 36); and the fief acknowledgment of Hans Forstmeister (von Gelnhausen), concerning his enfeoffment with Aufenau and Neudorf by Hans von Rodenstein, 1564 (item 38).

File note: Register of the start of proceedings: 1732.
